conclusion: The guard scripts/make_context.py --check catches its declared smallest mutant and all seventeen in-scope mutants tried, so its ledger entry can move from fired=None to fired=True. But it catches the declared mutant by accounting rather than comprehension — CONTEXT.md records a per-module line count, so a blank line alone fires it, while a public symbol added in a length-neutral edit to a module that declares __all__ (probe mutant B06) passes silently.
confidence: High on the outcome, which is a process exit code under two controls: the unmutated sandbox reproduces CONTEXT.md byte for byte, and the undo is re-checked after every one of 24 mutants. High on B06 being a real miss — it is a byte-identical regenerated artifact, not a judgment call. Lower on completeness: 24 mutants is a sample, not an enumeration, and I did not fuzz the ast parser or test concurrent edits. The four blind regions (meta/, compiler/, docs/doors/, non-test_* files) are facts about the globs; whether they are defects is a design question I did not answer.
operator_decision_required: Amending the guard ledger is a two-file edit outside this hunt's scope and needs a decision on both halves. (1) harness/departments/guard_ledger.py: set fired=True, demonstrated_by to this hunt's probe, scope to something like 'CONTEXT.md is a byte-exact function of zeta/, ontology/, harness/, dossier/, docs/*.md, scripts/*.py|*.sh and tests/test_*.py', and known_misses to the five candidates in RESULTS.md. (2) tests/test_guard_ledger.py::test_the_worklist_surfaces_the_undemonstrated_entries currently asserts this guard is STILL on the worklist, so it fails the moment the ledger is amended — that is the ledger working, but someone has to update the assertion in the same commit. Separately: hunts/README.md's case log has no r_414eed entry, and tests/test_hunt_probe_discipline.py::test_every_hunt_directory_is_covered_by_the_case_log requires one. Adding it means writing outside hunts/r_414eed/, which the brief forbade, so that test is expected to fail on this branch until a one-line entry is added.

threads.why_it_might_matter: A guard that fires on noise gets regenerated reflexively rather than read, and the same line-count sensitivity is what masks the one real miss (B06) by making almost every realistic edit fire for an unrelated reason.

core_candidates.what: A small reusable guard-mutation runner: copy the inputs a guard reads into a sandbox, assert the unmutated copy passes, apply one smallest-edit mutant, record the exit code, undo, re-assert quiet.
core_candidates.why_reusable: The guard ledger has seven records and two of them still read fired=None. Each needs exactly this loop, and the two controls (baseline-reproduces, undo-rechecked) are the part a hand-rolled demonstration is most likely to skip — without them a 'catch' can be an artefact of the copy or of the previous mutant. hunts/r_414eed/probe.py is that loop with the mutant list hard-coded.
core_candidates.first_step: Point the same harness at tests/test_doors.py, the other fired=None entry, whose declared mutant is 'a door command that no longer runs (renamed script)'.

core_candidates.what: Recording, per mutant, not just whether a guard fired but whether the mutated thing actually reached the guard's artifact.
core_candidates.why_reusable: It is the difference between a guard that works and a guard that happens to be correlated with the thing it claims to watch. Here it turned '17/17, guard is strong' into '17/17, and here is the edit shape that slips through'. Any ledger demonstration recording only an exit code can be wrong in exactly this way.
core_candidates.first_step: When amending guard_ledger.py, consider whether a demonstration record should be required to name the mechanism, not only the outcome.

notes_for_operator: Budget was spent on the question as asked plus a scope map, not on an install: the guard, the probe and CONTEXT.md are all pure standard library, so no .venv was built and no numerics ran. The one thing I deliberately left broken rather than fixed is the hunts/README.md case-log entry described in operator_decision_required — the brief's kill condition said to report rather than write outside hunts/r_414eed/, so I reported. operator-owned topic touched and not pursued: whether a demonstrated-guard amendment should be routine hunt output or a separate reviewed change is an allocation question, not a scientific one.
